name: Education
summary: AI labs ship study modes and fund training at scale, governments add AI to schooling, universities return to proctored exams, and trials suggest AI tutors help mainly when constrained and supervised.

regions.name: AI tutors
regions.summary: OpenAI and Google ship tutoring modes that guide rather than answer, and Khan Academy is building Khanmigo features on Gemini. Trials favor AI that works alongside human tutors.

landmarks.name: ChatGPT study mode
landmarks.summary: OpenAI launched a study mode that uses Socratic questions and step-by-step prompts instead of direct answers, for Free, Plus, Pro and Team users, with Edu to follow.
landmarks.note: openai.com blocks scripts; its RSS feed confirms launch date and purpose, not plan details.

landmarks.name: Gemini Guided Learning
landmarks.summary: Google added Guided Learning to the Gemini app, a mode built on its LearnLM models that asks questions, breaks problems into steps and uses images, videos and quizzes.

landmarks.name: Khan Academy builds Khanmigo tools on Gemini
landmarks.summary: After a partnership announced in January 2026, Khan Academy shipped Gemini-based interactive math and science diagrams and a rebuilt, teacher-reviewed practice tool in Khanmigo.

landmarks.name: Tutor CoPilot RCT
landmarks.summary: Preregistered trial with 900 tutors and 1,800 K-12 students: AI suggestions to human tutors raised topic mastery 4 points, and 9 for students of lower-rated tutors. Preprint.

regions.whyItMatters: Tutoring modes are how most students now meet AI, and their design decides whether it supports learning or replaces the effort.
regions.openQuestion: Will students choose a mode that makes them work when a direct answer is one click away?

deepDives.title: Tutor CoPilot study page (Stanford NSSA)
deepDives.why: Readable account of the human-plus-AI tutoring model and its measured effects.

deepDives.title: AI tutoring can safely and effectively support students: an exploratory RCT in UK classrooms
deepDives.why: How a tutor-supervised LearnLM was run and measured against human tutors in five UK schools.

deepDives.title: Towards Responsible Development of Generative AI for Education
deepDives.why: Google's account of how it turns learning-science principles into evaluations for tutoring models.

deepDives.title: Mathworlds (Dan Meyer)
deepDives.why: A math educator's skeptical running commentary on AI tutors and what classrooms actually use.

regions.name: Assessment & cheating
regions.summary: Universities are stepping back from AI detectors, which a New York court and several campuses have found unreliable as sole evidence, and returning to proctored, in-person exams.

landmarks.name: Princeton ends 133 years of unproctored exams
landmarks.summary: Princeton faculty voted with one dissent to proctor all in-class exams from 1 July 2026, the first time since its Honor Code began in 1893, citing cheating with generative AI.

landmarks.name: Stanford votes to allow exam proctoring
landmarks.summary: Stanford's Faculty Senate and both student legislatures voted to allow proctoring in all classes after a pilot, ending the unproctored norm set by its 1921 Honor Code.

landmarks.name: Curtin University turns off AI detection
landmarks.summary: Curtin in Australia said it would disable Turnitin's AI writing detection across all campuses from 1 January 2026, keeping regular text-matching checks. Announced September 2025.

landmarks.name: Court voids sanction based on Turnitin flag
landmarks.summary: In Newby v. Adelphi University, a New York judge ordered the university to reverse discipline and expunge the record of a student whose paper Turnitin flagged as wholly AI-written.
landmarks.note: Court site blocks scripts; read via a Feb 2026 report. Ruling month taken from the citation.

landmarks.name: HEPI survey: student AI use near universal
landmarks.summary: UK think tank HEPI's 2026 student survey found 95% use AI, 12% paste AI text into assessed work (3% in 2024), and 65% say assessment has changed significantly.

regions.whyItMatters: How schools verify that work is a student's own shapes what degrees certify and how much AI use is treated as misconduct.
regions.openQuestion: Can take-home and written coursework be assessed credibly at all, or only work done under supervision?

deepDives.title: Guidance on AI Detection and Why We're Disabling Turnitin's AI Detector (Vanderbilt)
deepDives.why: An early, widely cited explanation of the false-positive and transparency problems with detectors.

deepDives.title: Testing of Detection Tools for AI-Generated Text
deepDives.why: Independent test of detection tools by integrity researchers; a standard reference on their limits.

deepDives.title: GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers
deepDives.why: Stanford study showing detectors misflag writing by non-native English speakers.

deepDives.title: The Cheat Sheet (Derek Newton)
deepDives.why: Regular newsletter on academic integrity and cheating; often argues the pro-detection side.

regions.name: School & university policy
regions.summary: Governments are requiring AI education in schools and giving students and teachers access to AI tools, often in partnership with AI companies.

landmarks.name: US executive order on AI education
landmarks.summary: EO 14277 created a White House task force on AI education, called for a Presidential AI Challenge and told the Education Department to prioritize AI in teacher training grants.

landmarks.name: Beijing requires AI classes in schools
landmarks.summary: Beijing's education commission said primary and secondary schools would offer at least eight class hours of AI instruction a year from the fall 2025 semester.

landmarks.name: Estonia announces AI Leap
landmarks.summary: Estonia announced free AI tools for 20,000 students in grades 10-11 and 3,000 teachers from September 2025, in talks with OpenAI and Anthropic, with 38,000 more students in 2026.

regions.whyItMatters: National mandates and vendor partnerships set which AI tools a generation of students grows up using, and on whose terms.
regions.openQuestion: Do national rollouts improve learning, or mainly lock school systems into particular vendors?

deepDives.title: Guidance for generative AI in education and research (UNESCO)
deepDives.why: UNESCO's first global guidance on generative AI in education, including regulation steps and age limits.

deepDives.title: State AI Guidance for K12 Schools (AI for Education)
deepDives.why: Running list of US states with official K-12 AI guidance, with summaries and links to each.

deepDives.title: AI Guidance for Schools Toolkit (TeachAI)
deepDives.why: Widely used template and principles for education authorities writing their own AI guidance.

deepDives.title: Estonia: AI Leap Initiative to Enhance Learning and Teaching (Eurydice)
deepDives.why: EU education network's summary of how Estonia structured its national AI rollout.

regions.name: Upskilling & workforce learning
regions.summary: AI companies are funding large training programs and credentials for workers and teachers, with stated goals in the tens of millions of people. Outcomes are not yet measured.

landmarks.name: Microsoft Elevate $4B commitment
landmarks.summary: Microsoft pledged over $4B in cash and technology over five years to schools and nonprofits, and said Elevate Academy would help 20 million people earn AI credentials in two years.

landmarks.name: OpenAI certifications and jobs platform
landmarks.summary: OpenAI announced AI certifications through OpenAI Academy and plans for a jobs platform by mid-2026, committing to certify 10 million Americans by 2030 with Walmart as a partner.
landmarks.note: openai.com blocks scripts; its RSS feed confirms the announcement and date, not the targets.

landmarks.name: AFT National Academy for AI Instruction
landmarks.summary: Teachers union AFT announced a $23M academy in New York funded by Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic, offering free AI training and aiming to reach 400,000 educators in five years.

regions.whyItMatters: Vendor-funded training is becoming the main route by which workers and teachers learn AI, which shapes what counts as AI skill.
regions.openQuestion: Do vendor-issued AI credentials lead to better jobs or teaching, and who checks that independently?

deepDives.title: AILit Framework (European Commission and OECD)
deepDives.why: Joint AI literacy framework for schools that feeds into the PISA 2029 assessment.

deepDives.title: Education chapter, 2026 AI Index Report (Stanford HAI)
deepDives.why: Annual independent data on AI degrees, school policies and AI skills acquired outside formal education.

deepDives.title: Elements of AI
deepDives.why: Free non-vendor introduction to AI from the University of Helsinki and MinnaLearn.

deepDives.title: Microsoft, OpenAI Partner With AFT to Train Teachers on AI (Education Week)
deepDives.why: Independent reporting on the academy, with outside views on vendor-funded teacher training.

regions.name: Evidence on learning outcomes
regions.summary: Controlled trials are accumulating. Unrestricted chatbots can hurt later unaided performance; constrained, supervised tutors show gains in short studies but not yet on broad tests.

landmarks.name: Unguarded AI can harm learning (PNAS)
landmarks.summary: Field experiment with nearly 1,000 high school math students: once access ended, GPT-4 users scored 17% worse than peers who never had it. A guardrailed tutor mostly avoided this.

landmarks.name: Harvard physics AI tutor RCT
landmarks.summary: Crossover RCT in Scientific Reports (N=194): median learning gains with a custom AI tutor were over double those in an active learning class, in less time. Two lessons only.

landmarks.name: Eedi and Google DeepMind 10-week RCT
landmarks.summary: Trial with 1,179 students in 10 UK schools: supervised AI tutoring matched human tutors in lessons (56-58% correct vs 43% for static content) but showed no gain on a standard test.
landmarks.note: Eedi press release on its own trial; follows a 165-student exploratory study (arXiv 2512.23633).

landmarks.name: World Bank GPT-4 tutoring RCT in Nigeria
landmarks.summary: Randomized trial of a six-week, teacher-supported after-school program using GPT-4 in Edo State found gains of 0.31 standard deviations overall and 0.23 in English. Working paper.

regions.whyItMatters: Billions are being spent on AI in classrooms on the strength of a handful of short trials, so what the evidence shows matters.
regions.openQuestion: Do gains from constrained AI tutors persist over a school year, show up on broad tests and replicate outside supervised trials?

deepDives.title: OECD Digital Education Outlook 2026
deepDives.why: Synthesis of the trial evidence, separating general chatbots from purpose-built education tools.

deepDives.title: Research Study Repository (Stanford SCALE)
deepDives.why: Searchable collection of academic studies on generative AI in preK-12 education.

deepDives.title: A new direction for students in an AI world: Prosper, prepare, protect (Brookings)
deepDives.why: Year-long global study of the risks generative AI poses to students and how to reduce them.

deepDives.title: Your Brain on ChatGPT (MIT Media Lab preprint)
deepDives.why: Much cited 54-person EEG study of essay writing with an LLM; not peer reviewed, read with care.

deepDives.title: OECD Digital Education Outlook 2026
deepDives.why: Cross-country review of what generative AI does and does not do for learning, teaching and administration.

deepDives.title: Research Study Repository (Stanford SCALE)
deepDives.why: The place to check what studies exist on generative AI in schools before trusting a headline.

deepDives.title: Education chapter, 2026 AI Index Report (Stanford HAI)
deepDives.why: Yearly data on student AI use, school policies, national AI curricula and AI graduates.

deepDives.title: Guidance for generative AI in education and research (UNESCO)
deepDives.why: The reference global policy guidance, used by many ministries as a starting point.

deepDives.title: One Useful Thing (Ethan Mollick)
deepDives.why: Wharton professor's widely read newsletter on what AI means for work, education and life.
